title: Words Given to Malachi
summary: Jesus commands the people to write the words the Father gave Malachi, expounds them after they are written, and begins speaking them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus commanded the people to write the words the Father had given to Malachi.
After the words were written, Jesus expounded them and began to tell them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people write as Jesus addresses them.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and arrangement of the people, writing materials, and setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I will send my messenger,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: he commanded them that they should write the words

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy is being spoken by Jesus, quoting words given by the Father to Malachi.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Malachi or the prophesied messenger as physically present.

title: The Messenger and the Coming Lord
summary: The quoted prophecy tells of a messenger preparing the way and the Lord suddenly coming to his temple.

explicit_facts.text: The prophecy says a messenger will prepare the way before the Lord, who will suddenly come to his temple.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use symbolic or written imagery rather than showing the messenger or Lord as present characters.
unspecified_visual_details: The messenger’s identity and appearance; the temple’s appearance; the manner of the Lord’s coming.

spoken_dialogue.text: he shall prepare the way before me,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: the Lord whom ye seek shall suddenly come to his temple

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy reports a future event; do not portray it as happening in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent appearances or stage a visible arrival.

title: The Day of His Coming
summary: The prophecy asks who can endure the day of the Lord’s coming, comparing him to refining fire and fuller’s soap, and says he will purify the sons of Levi.

explicit_facts.text: The prophecy asks who may abide the day of his coming and who shall stand when he appears.
He is compared to a refiner’s fire and fuller’s soap, and is said to purify the sons of Levi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Metaphorical imagery may suggest refining and cleansing without depicting a literal supernatural event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the Lord and the sons of Levi.

spoken_dialogue.text: who may abide the day of his coming,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fire and soap are figures of speech; do not portray them as literal acts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal refining scene or invent the Lord’s appearance.

title: An Offering in Righteousness
summary: The prophecy says the sons of Levi will offer in righteousness, and Judah and Jerusalem’s offering will be pleasant to the Lord as in former days.

explicit_facts.text: The sons of Levi are to offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.
The offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to the Lord as in former years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic offering may represent the prophecy, without specifying its form.
unspecified_visual_details: The offering’s form, participants’ appearances, and location.

spoken_dialogue.text: that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: Then shall the offering of Judah and Jerusalem be pleasant unto the Lord,

prohibited_inventions: Do not specify a sacrificial rite or portray a distinct historical event.

title: A Swift Witness in Judgment
summary: The prophecy says the Lord will come near to judge and witness against wrongdoing and oppression.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he will come near to judgment and be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, those who oppress hired workers, widows and fatherless people, and those who turn aside strangers and do not fear him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Represent the listed wrongs symbolically rather than inventing specific incidents or people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people involved, setting, and form of judgment.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will come near to you to judgment;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: against those that oppress the hireling in his wages,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophetic warning, not a narrated present-tense judgment event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray a specific judgment or identify unnamed wrongdoers.

title: The Lord Changes Not
summary: The Lord declares that he does not change and calls the people to return to him; they ask how they should return.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he does not change and that the sons of Jacob are not consumed.
The Lord says the people have departed from his ordinances and calls them to return; they ask, “Wherein shall we return?”

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the words as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the people addressed.

spoken_dialogue.text: Return unto me and I will return unto you,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi
The people addressed in the prophecy

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people’s question is reported in the prophecy; no individual speaker is identified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add visible interlocutors or stage an unreported encounter.

title: Tithes and Offerings
summary: The prophecy accuses the people of robbing God in tithes and offerings and says the whole nation is cursed with a curse.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord asks whether a man will rob God and says the people have robbed him in tithes and offerings.
The Lord says the whole nation is cursed with a curse because it has robbed him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use symbolic imagery of tithes or offerings without depicting a specific act of theft.
unspecified_visual_details: The offerings, storehouse, and people’s appearances.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a scene of theft or a visible curse.

title: Bring the Tithes
summary: The prophecy commands the people to bring all tithes into the storehouse and promises a blessing from heaven.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commands the people to bring all tithes into the storehouse so there may be meat in his house.
The Lord invites them to prove him and promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing beyond room to receive it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The storehouse and blessing may be suggested symbolically; the promised action is not narrated as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The storehouse’s appearance and the nature of the blessing.

spoken_dialogue.text: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised blessing is future and should not be staged as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict heaven opening or invent a specific blessing.

title: The Fruits of the Ground
summary: The Lord promises to rebuke the devourer so crops and vines are not destroyed, and says all nations will call the people blessed.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord promises to rebuke the devourer so it will not destroy the fruits of the ground or cause the vine to cast its fruit before its time.
All nations will call the people blessed, and their land will be delightsome.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic view of fruitful land may illustrate the promise.
unspecified_visual_details: The land’s appearance, the devourer’s identity, and the nations’ identities.

spoken_dialogue.text: neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

narration.text: ye shall be a delightsome land,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are promises, not events described as occurring in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal devourer or an enacted miracle.

title: Words Against the Lord
summary: The Lord says the people have spoken stoutly against him. Their reported words question the profit of serving God and call the proud happy.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says the people’s words have been stout against him, and they ask what they have said against him.
They have said it is vain to serve God and questioned the profit of keeping ordinances and walking mournfully before the Lord.
They call the proud happy and say that those who work wickedness are set up and those who tempt God are delivered.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the accusation and reported words as off-screen speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those whose words are reported.

spoken_dialogue.text: It is vain to serve God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The people whose words are reported in the prophecy

narration.text: Your words have been stout against me,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The words are reported speech, not a new present-tense conversation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent individual speakers or depict specific acts of wickedness.

title: A Book of Remembrance
summary: Those who feared the Lord spoke often to one another; the Lord heard, and a book of remembrance was written for them. The Lord says they will be his and he will spare them.

explicit_facts.text: Those who feared the Lord spoke often to one another, and the Lord hearkened and heard.
A book of remembrance was written before the Lord for those who feared him and thought upon his name.
The Lord says they will be his when he makes up his jewels and that he will spare them as a man spares his serving son.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people speaking to one another and a book being written are described actions; avoid depicting the Lord, whose appearance is unspecified.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities and appearance, and the book’s appearance.

spoken_dialogue.text: Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Narration within the prophecy

narration.text: a book of remembrance was written before him

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Make up my jewels” and the comparison to a man sparing his son are figurative language.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a heavenly figure or literal jewels.

title: Discern Between the Righteous and the Wicked
summary: The prophecy says the people will return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between those who serve God and those who do not.

explicit_facts.text: The people will return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, and between those who serve God and those who do not.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use a symbolic contrast to convey discernment without assigning identities or depicting specific deeds.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, setting, and visual form of the contrast.

spoken_dialogue.text: Then shall ye return and discern
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful), quoting the Father’s words to Malachi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy describes a future discernment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unreported judgment scene or identify individuals as righteous or wicked.
